BiblicalUsage: Cyrus was the Persian king who conquered Babylon and then did what no conqueror before him had done: he sent God's people home. In the first year of his reign he made a decree to rebuild the house of God at Jerusalem, as the record found in Ezra 6:3 sets out, he returned the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken in Ezra 5:13, and Daniel prospered in his reign in Daniel 6:28.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simply that Cyrus is the proof that God rules over kings who do not know Him: He named Cyrus long before he was born, and used a pagan emperor to open the way home.
